stretch: Stand up and reach for the ceiling.
Roll your shoulders, shake out your wrists, look out a window.
Stretch your back, your neck and your fingers. 30 seconds is plenty.
Unfold yourself. Your spine will thank you.
Look at something far away for 20 seconds. Your eyes have been staring at a rectangle.
Shrug your shoulders up to your ears, hold, then drop them. Repeat.
Interlace your fingers, flip your palms out, and push. Your wrists have earned it.
Slowly tilt your head toward each shoulder. The keyboard is not a shoulder.
Stand up and touch your toes, or at least wave in their general direction.
Twist gently to the left, then the right. Your chair has had enough of you.
Blink. Slowly. A few times. Your eyes will be grateful.
Open and close your hands ten times. Typing muscles need a different workout.
Walk to the farthest window and say hello to the sky.
Do a slow neck roll. Ignore any crunchy noises.
Stand on one foot for a bit, then switch. Congratulations, you're a flamingo.
Reach behind you and give your chest a good opening stretch.
Take three slow, deep breaths. The code will wait.
Your posture called. It wants a word. Sit up, then get up.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together like you're holding a pencil between them.
Stretch your forearms: arm out, palm up, gently pull the fingers back.
Roll your ankles. They've been in witness protection under the desk.
Stand up and do a lap. Even a short one counts.
Your hip flexors have been folded for ages. Stand up and let them out.
Rub your hands together, then cup them over your closed eyes for a moment.
Stretch like a cat: long, slow, and entirely without shame.
Grab some water on the way back. Hydrate while you un-hunch.
Raise both arms overhead, lean left, lean right. You are a very tall teapot.
Make a fist, release, and spread your fingers wide. Repeat until your hands feel less like claws.
Unclench your jaw. Yes, that one. Right now.
Put your palms on a wall and lean in to stretch your calves. Ignore the neighbors.
Pretend you're hanging a very tall picture. Both arms, all the way up.
Look left, look right, look up, look down. The room is still there, mostly.
Give your wrists a little circle each way. They do a lot for you.
Stand, stretch, wiggle. Nobody is watching. Probably.
